refs.name: Chicago
refs.blurb: Start of every drive estimate (the Loop). The 4-hour ring is the near edge of the brief: everything inside it is weekend-cottage country, not the archetype.

refs.name: Trout Lake (the archetype)
refs.blurb: The reference point, and the one lake here you already know. 3,816 acres, 117 ft deep, gin-clear, wrapped almost entirely by the 236,000-acre Northern Highland–American Legion State Forest. Almost no private frontage exists — and none was for sale this month.

lakes.name: Black Oak Lake
lakes.clarity: Widely cited as Wisconsin's clearest — Secchi routinely 25–30 ft. 85 ft max, 34 ft mean.
lakes.motors: Full-motor lake, no horsepower cap. Skiing legal and practiced; small landing keeps traffic low.
lakes.blurb: The clearest water in the state and the closest thing here to Squam's gin-clarity. Sub-bar at 564 acres — a real constraint for five boats — but the water quality is unmatched and the culture is old Land O'Lakes camps. Inventory is famously thin; one 3BR is live at $699K.

lakes.name: Presque Isle Lake
lakes.clarity: Clear, deep (103 ft), spring-fed; among the better Vilas readings.
lakes.motors: Full motor; the town's ethos is quiet, and the lake sits at the end of the road.
lakes.blurb: 1,165 acres and 103 feet deep at the top-left corner of Vilas County, half an hour past where day-trippers turn around. State and county forest on much of the shore, an understated summer-camp culture, and a market that actually trades — 30 active listings countywide this summer, average ask ~$520K.

lakes.name: Big Muskellunge Lake
lakes.clarity: Clear; part of the NTL-LTER long-term research set (the most-studied water in the Midwest). 70 ft max.
lakes.motors: Full motor, no horsepower cap; NHAL landing only.
lakes.blurb: Trout Lake's smaller neighbor, and nearly its equal on water: deep, clear, forest-ringed. Same problem — state forest owns most of the shore, so listings are events, not inventory. Set alerts and be ready.

lakes.name: Plum Lake
lakes.clarity: DNR classifies it very clear; 57 ft max.
lakes.motors: Full motor; connected to Big St. Germain via the Plum–Star chain.
lakes.blurb: Sayner's lake, and one of the oldest continuous summer colonies in the Northwoods — the kind of place where the same six families have held frontage since the 1890s. Clear water, decent size, and a real (if small) market. Plum Lake Public Library and the Sayner store are the entire downtown.

lakes.name: Star Lake
lakes.clarity: Clear, 68 ft max; long-term monitoring by the Plum–Star association.
lakes.motors: Full motor; NHAL forest landing, no marina.
lakes.blurb: 1,206 acres inside the state forest, with the historic Star Lake hamlet (population ~40) at one end and virtually nothing at the other. The quietest big water in Vilas County that still has private frontage on it.

lakes.name: North Twin Lake
lakes.clarity: Moderately clear; 60 ft max, 28 ft mean. Class-A musky water.
lakes.motors: Full motor, no cap; connected by channel to South Twin (628 ac, very clear).
lakes.blurb: Phelps' big lake — 2,871 acres with real running room, a channel to a clearer 628-acre second basin, and the most active high-end frontage market in the county (a 61-acre, 1,022-ft assemblage listed at $5.2M this year). Also home to a live 1897 resort at $2.8M.

lakes.name: Long Lake (Phelps)
lakes.clarity: Clear and unusually deep for its size — 88 ft max.
lakes.motors: Full motor; quiet, few public amenities.
lakes.blurb: 886 acres and 88 feet deep east of Phelps, hard against the Michigan line and the Nicolet National Forest. Deep-and-clear on a small footprint; the trade is a shorter ski fetch.

lakes.name: Lac Vieux Desert
lakes.clarity: Moderately clear; shallow for its size (38 ft max) so it warms and colors by August.
lakes.motors: Full motor; straddles the state line — carry both registrations if you keep a boat here.
lakes.blurb: The headwater of the Wisconsin River, 4,017 acres straddling the border at Land O'Lakes. Plenty of water for five boats and prices well under the Vilas average, but it is not archetype-clear — mark it a size-and-value play, not a water play.

lakes.name: Big St. Germain Lake
lakes.clarity: Moderately clear; 42 ft max.
lakes.motors: Full motor; busy channel to Little St. Germain.
lakes.blurb: 1,617 acres with a genuine ski culture and the best restaurant density in the region. Honest tradeoff: this is the Northwoods at its most trafficked — pontoon-heavy weekends, a big landing, and a bar-and-grill shoreline. Program-friendly, atmosphere-compromised.

lakes.name: Big Arbor Vitae Lake
lakes.clarity: Moderate; 42 ft max, weedier bays.
lakes.motors: Full motor; heavy summer traffic from Woodruff/Minocqua.
lakes.blurb: 1,070 acres 10 minutes from Minocqua — which is exactly the problem. Listed for completeness and for the one live 34.5-acre multi-dwelling property on it ($3.25M).

lakes.name: High & Fishtrap Lakes
lakes.clarity: Clear; part of the Headwaters chain.
lakes.motors: Full motor; connected chain, low traffic.
lakes.blurb: A quiet connected chain between Land O'Lakes and Boulder Junction, deep in the forest. A live 5BR/3.5BA on High Lake at $1.03M is the sort of beachhead this strategy wants.

lakes.name: Big Portage Lake
lakes.clarity: Moderately clear.
lakes.motors: Full motor.
lakes.blurb: 1,000 quiet acres northeast of Boulder Junction with state forest holdings on part of the shore. Modest inventory; a reasonable second-choice if the Trout/Muskellunge cluster stays dry.

lakes.name: Fence Lake (Lac du Flambeau chain)
lakes.clarity: Moderate; the chain's ten lakes vary widely.
lakes.motors: Full motor, big connected chain — the most ski-friendly water in the county.
lakes.blurb: 3,555 acres on the ten-lake Lac du Flambeau chain: unmatched cruising, genuinely mixed water quality, and a shoreline substantially within the Lac du Flambeau Band's reservation, where non-member purchase and leasing rules are their own diligence project. Enter only with counsel who has done it before.

lakes.name: Lac du Lune
lakes.clarity: Clear.
lakes.motors: Full motor; very low traffic.
lakes.blurb: Small (470 ac) but clear and almost undeveloped, near Land O'Lakes. On the list only because of one extraordinary listing: 27+ acres with 1,181 ft of frontage at $1.35M — the largest single-owner frontage assemblage found in Vilas County this sweep.

lakes.name: Dunn Lake
lakes.clarity: Clear, small.
lakes.motors: Full motor but too small to ski properly.
lakes.blurb: Well under the size bar and included for one reason: a 14+ acre parcel with over 1,000 ft of frontage at $347.5K. Cheapest big-frontage canvas in the sweep — pair it with boat storage on Presque Isle Lake, five minutes away.

lakes.name: Lake Tomahawk
lakes.clarity: Clear; 84 ft max — one of the deeper big lakes in Oneida County.
lakes.motors: Full motor, no cap. Real ski culture; slow-no-wake within 100 ft of shore.
lakes.blurb: The best size-clarity-drive combination in Wisconsin: 3,392 acres, 84 feet deep, an hour closer than the Vilas cluster, and a market with actual compound-scale product — a legacy estate with main home plus furnished cabins and multiple docks is live at $3.3M. Busier than Trout, quieter than Minocqua.

lakes.name: Willow Flowage
lakes.clarity: Moderately clear, tannin-tinted; shallow at 30 ft max.
lakes.motors: Full motor; no wake within 100 ft. Very few docks, almost no development.
lakes.blurb: 6,306 acres of state-designated Scenic Waters — the most undeveloped big water within 5½ hours of Chicago, with eagles, no shoreline lighting, and a drawdown regime. Frontage is scarce because the state owns most of it, and the water is bog-tinted rather than clear. Pure atmosphere, compromised on the water bar.

lakes.name: Squirrel Lake
lakes.clarity: Moderately clear; 46 ft max.
lakes.motors: Full motor; modest traffic.
lakes.blurb: 1,309 quiet acres between Minocqua and Lac du Flambeau with a low-key camp shoreline and prices below the Minocqua premium. A sensible value fallback.

lakes.name: Two Sisters Lake
lakes.clarity: Clear; county forest on part of the shore.
lakes.motors: Full motor.
lakes.blurb: 719 clear acres ringed partly by Oneida County forest. Under the size bar for five boats but a strong second lake if you buy nearby.

lakes.name: Pelican Lake
lakes.clarity: Moderate; 40 ft max.
lakes.motors: Full motor, no cap; the closest genuinely big ski lake to Chicago in this report.
lakes.blurb: 3,585 acres at five hours flat — the best drive-to-size ratio in Wisconsin. The water is good rather than elite and the shore is more developed than Vilas, but a nine-acre resort with 204 ft of frontage is live here at $724.9K, which is compound math almost nobody else offers.

lakes.name: Sugar Camp Chain
lakes.clarity: Mixed across the five lakes.
lakes.motors: Full motor; connected chain.
lakes.blurb: Five connected lakes northeast of Rhinelander with real cruising and a live $1.499M frontage listing. Water quality varies lake to lake — sample before you commit.

lakes.name: Turtle–Flambeau Flowage
lakes.clarity: Moderately clear, tannin-stained; ~50 ft max.
lakes.motors: Full motor; 195 islands and enormous open water. Slow-no-wake near shore only.
lakes.blurb: Wisconsin's seventh-largest lake and its wildest — 12,942 acres, 195 islands, and a state Scenic Waters designation that keeps virtually the entire shoreline undeveloped. If your five couples want the feeling of being alone on big water, nothing in this report beats it. The water is tea-colored, not gin: an honest, deliberate trade.

lakes.name: Pike Lake Chain
lakes.clarity: Moderately clear.
lakes.motors: Full motor; five connected lakes.
lakes.blurb: A quiet five-lake chain outside Mercer with low prices and low traffic. Not archetype water, but the cheapest connected cruising in the sweep.

lakes.name: Lake Metonga
lakes.clarity: Clear; 80 ft max — one of the clearest lakes in the Nicolet.
lakes.motors: Full motor, no cap.
lakes.blurb: 2,157 acres and 80 feet deep at Crandon, five and a quarter hours out — clear, deep, underpriced, and almost entirely absent from Chicago's mental map of the Northwoods. The sweep's best-kept secret on the Wisconsin side.

lakes.name: Franklin & Butternut Lakes
lakes.clarity: Franklin is notably clear (spring-fed, 65 ft); Butternut is larger and moderate.
lakes.motors: Full motor on Butternut; Franklin is small and quiet.
lakes.blurb: The Anvil/Franklin corner of the Chequamegon-Nicolet National Forest east of Eagle River: federal forest on nearly all the shoreline, old CCC-era camps, and the best hiking within a mile of the water anywhere in this report.

lakes.name: Grindstone Lake
lakes.clarity: Elite — Secchi averaged 23 ft across 1993–2005 monitoring. 60 ft max, 10.5 mi of shoreline.
lakes.motors: Full motor, no cap; low traffic, one landing. Skiing legal and normal.
lakes.blurb: The truest Squam analog west of Lake Michigan: 3,176 acres, thirteen years of 23-foot Secchi readings, sand beaches, and a shoreline shared between old family camps and the Lac Courte Oreilles Band. Big enough for five boats, quiet enough to hear loons at noon. Live inventory exists — a chalet-plus-guest-cottage pairing is on the market now.

lakes.name: Lac Courte Oreilles
lakes.clarity: Very clear per DNR; 90 ft max, 25.4 mi of shoreline.
lakes.motors: Full motor, no cap; big enough that traffic disperses.
lakes.blurb: 5,039 acres and 90 feet deep — the largest genuinely clear ski lake in this report that still trades at compound prices. Twenty-five miles of shoreline means real variety: quiet coves, sand beaches, and one legacy estate live at $2.495M with 10.82 acres and 320 ft of level sand. Note the reservation boundary and title questions on parts of the shore; use a Hayward attorney.

lakes.name: Round Lake
lakes.clarity: Clear; 74 ft max, ~33 ft mean.
lakes.motors: Full motor, no cap; Chequamegon National Forest shoreline keeps development low.
lakes.blurb: 3,294 acres wrapped by national forest northeast of Hayward — the buildable Trout Lake. Two live paths at once: a cabin-and-guest-cottage at $1.95M, and Moose Jaw Resort — 17 acres of federal-forest-adjacent frontage with a working cabin cluster — at $2.75M.

lakes.name: Teal & Lost Land Lakes
lakes.clarity: Moderately clear; connected pair.
lakes.motors: Full motor; connected by a navigable thoroughfare.
lakes.blurb: A connected 2,300-acre pair inside the Chequamegon National Forest, historically resort country — which means grandfathered cabin clusters, the exact product this brief is hunting.

lakes.name: Spider Lake Chain
lakes.clarity: Moderately clear across the five basins.
lakes.motors: Full motor; connected chain.
lakes.blurb: Five connected lakes in the national forest north of Hayward with an old resort economy and one of the highest densities of multi-cabin properties in the state.

lakes.name: Chippewa Flowage
lakes.clarity: Moderate, tannin-stained; 92 ft max.
lakes.motors: Full motor; 200+ miles of shoreline, most of it undeveloped.
lakes.blurb: 15,300 acres, 140 islands, and more than 200 miles of shoreline that will never be built on — Wisconsin's third-largest lake and its most convincing wilderness. Stumps, drawdowns and stained water are the price of admission; five couples who want scale over sparkle should look hard here.

lakes.name: Big Sissabagama Lake
lakes.clarity: Clear; 48 ft max.
lakes.motors: Full motor.
lakes.blurb: 805 clear acres near Stone Lake with a quiet, almost entirely residential shore. Under the size bar; a good second lake.

lakes.name: Nelson Lake
lakes.clarity: Stained and shallow — fails the water bar.
lakes.motors: Full motor; wide open.
lakes.blurb: 2,500 acres of cheap frontage near Hayward. Big and boat-friendly, but tea-dark and shallow. In the report for price transparency, not as a recommendation.

lakes.name: Lake Owen
lakes.clarity: Elite — Secchi ~24.6 ft, graded A. 95 ft max. DNR classifies it very clear.
lakes.motors: Full motor, no cap; Chequamegon National Forest landing, minimal traffic.
lakes.blurb: The northern jewel: 1,250 acres, 95 feet deep, 24.6-foot clarity, and national forest on most of the shore south of Cable. Smaller than the bar wants and priced accordingly at the top (a 5.3-acre, 350-ft retreat is asking $3M) — but the water and the hush are Squam-grade.

lakes.name: Lake Namakagon
lakes.clarity: Clear; shallow-ish for its size at 51 ft max, 16 ft mean.
lakes.motors: Full motor, no cap; national forest shoreline.
lakes.blurb: 2,897 acres in the Chequamegon-Nicolet National Forest above Cable — the headwater of the Namekagon National Scenic Riverway, with real running room and prices well under the Vilas/Antrim premium (Bayfield County average ask ~$627K). Shallower than the depth-lovers want.

lakes.name: Eau Claire Lakes chain
lakes.clarity: Clear; three connected basins with sand bottoms.
lakes.motors: Full motor; connected chain, low traffic.
lakes.blurb: Three connected clear-water basins in far Bayfield County — sand bottoms, pines, and almost no through traffic. Sub-bar individually, credible as a chain.

lakes.name: Lake Nebagamon
lakes.clarity: Clear; sand-bottomed.
lakes.motors: Full motor; village lake with a genuine summer-colony culture.
lakes.blurb: 981 acres and a hundred-year-old summer village an hour from Duluth. Sub-bar on size but archetype-grade on culture, and among the cheapest clear frontage in the sweep.

lakes.name: Crystal Lake
lakes.clarity: Elite — marl-bottomed, 165 ft max, 70 ft mean; the 'Caribbean of the North'.
lakes.motors: Full motor, no cap; Michigan's statewide no-wake band is 100 ft from shore / under 3 ft depth.
lakes.blurb: Michigan's ninth-largest inland lake and one of its two clearest: 9,854 acres, 165 feet deep, 21 miles of shoreline, and turquoise water over white marl. Five and a quarter hours from the Loop — the best water-to-drive ratio in this entire report. The trade is price and pace: Beulah frontage runs $1.2M–$1.9M for ordinary cottages, and a compound means assembling.

lakes.name: Big Glen Lake
lakes.clarity: Excellent — Secchi just over 19 ft in the Leelanau Conservancy dataset; 130 ft max.
lakes.motors: Full motor, no cap; the narrows to Little Glen are no-wake.
lakes.blurb: 4,871 acres inside Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore — federal land on a large share of the shore, water that photographs like the Caribbean, and dunes for a backdrop. The most beautiful lake in this report. Also among the most expensive and the most supply-constrained: very few homes trade in any year, and $3M is an ordinary ask.

lakes.name: Lake Leelanau (N & S)
lakes.clarity: Good; North basin 121 ft max, South 62 ft.
lakes.motors: Full motor; the narrows at Leland Township are no-wake. Active wake-boat debate — Lake Leelanau Lake Association is a lead advocate for 500-ft setbacks.
lakes.blurb: 8,607 acres across two connected basins in the middle of Leelanau's wine country — big water, good clarity, real running room, and a shore that mixes orchards with cottages. Cheaper than Glen, busier than Crystal.
links: Lake Leelanau Association on wake boats

lakes.name: Long Lake (Grand Traverse)
lakes.clarity: Good; deep basins, sand bottom, several islands.
lakes.motors: Full motor; township ordinances govern speed near the islands.
lakes.blurb: 2,860 acres and several wooded islands twenty minutes west of Traverse City. Clear sand-bottom water, established cottage culture, and — unusually for the region — enough size for five boats without feeling like a highway.

lakes.name: Big Platte Lake
lakes.clarity: Good; the subject of a decades-long, court-supervised phosphorus cleanup that worked.
lakes.motors: Full motor; Sleeping Bear National Lakeshore adjoins.
lakes.blurb: 2,517 acres beside Sleeping Bear, with a shoreline association that litigated its way to clean water and won. Quieter and cheaper than Glen or Crystal, and a real ski lake.

lakes.name: Portage Lake (Onekama)
lakes.clarity: Good; channel to Lake Michigan.
lakes.motors: Full motor; a working channel to Lake Michigan means a mixed fleet.
lakes.blurb: 2,110 acres with its own channel to Lake Michigan — the only lake in this report where you can ski all morning and run to big water in the afternoon. Under five hours out. The channel is also the caveat: this is a boating lake, not a hushed one.

lakes.name: Hamlin Lake
lakes.clarity: Moderate; shallow upper basin, dark water in the narrows.
lakes.motors: Full motor; Ludington State Park landing draws real crowds.
lakes.blurb: 4,990 acres at four and a half hours — the closest big lake that clears the drive floor. Good boating, ordinary water, and state-park traffic all summer. A convenience play, not an archetype one.

lakes.name: Elk Lake
lakes.clarity: Elite — 192 ft max, oligotrophic, part of the Elk River Chain of Lakes monitoring program.
lakes.motors: Full motor, no cap; quieter than neighboring Torch by a wide margin.
lakes.blurb: Torch Lake's water without Torch Lake's sandbar. 7,730 acres, 192 feet deep, the same improbable blue, and a shoreline of old cottages rather than party barges — plus a connection through the Chain of Lakes to Torch and Bellaire when you want the scene. The strongest single lake on the Michigan side.

lakes.name: Torch Lake
lakes.clarity: Elite on paper — 330 ft max, 111 ft mean, ranked among the clearest lakes in the Western Hemisphere.
lakes.motors: Full motor, no cap; the sandbar at the south end is a nationally known party anchorage on summer weekends.
lakes.blurb: The most beautiful water in the Midwest and the least Squam-like culture in this report. 18,770 acres of turquoise over marl — and, on a July Saturday, several hundred rafted boats on the south sandbar. Buy on the quiet northeast shore or don't buy here; a 14-acre, 4BR at $999K shows it can be done.

lakes.name: Lake Bellaire
lakes.clarity: Good; 96 ft max, part of the Chain of Lakes.
lakes.motors: Full motor; connected to Torch via the Torch River / Clam River.
lakes.blurb: 1,775 acres at the quiet end of the Antrim chain: clear enough, deep enough, connected to everything, and priced meaningfully below Torch or Elk. The value entry into the Chain of Lakes.

lakes.name: Intermediate Lake
lakes.clarity: Moderate; shallower and more colored than its neighbors.
lakes.motors: Full motor; chain-connected.
lakes.blurb: 1,520 acres at the top of the Antrim chain, notably cheaper than the lakes below it — and notably less clear. A budget route onto the chain.

lakes.name: Lake Charlevoix
lakes.clarity: Good to very good; 122 ft max, channel to Lake Michigan.
lakes.motors: Full motor; the South Arm is markedly quieter than the main basin.
lakes.blurb: 17,260 acres, a Lake Michigan channel, and Boyne City and Charlevoix on its shores — the Midwest's Lake Winnipesaukee, with the same virtues and the same crowding. The South Arm is the play: median frontage runs ~$2,450/ft there against $7,000–$12,000/ft on the main basin.

lakes.name: Walloon Lake
lakes.clarity: Elite — oligotrophic, visibility frequently over 20 ft, 100 ft max.
lakes.motors: Full motor, no cap; no public marina, one modest launch, and a shoreline culture that polices its own noise.
lakes.blurb: The Squam of the Midwest, in every sense including price. 4,584 acres of oligotrophic water, Hemingway's boyhood lake, no commercial shoreline, and generational owners who do not sell. Twelve listings totalled $64.7M this summer; entry cottages start in the mid-$800Ks and the good frontage is $7M+. Include it, tour it, and know the odds.
links: Tip of the Mitt — Walloon Lake

lakes.name: Crooked & Pickerel Lakes
lakes.clarity: Good; Pickerel is the deeper and clearer of the pair.
lakes.motors: Full motor; the Inland Waterway connects them to Burt, Mullett and Lake Huron.
lakes.blurb: 3,450 combined acres at the west end of the Inland Waterway — the 38-mile chain that runs from Conway to Cheboygan and out to Lake Huron. Quiet, forested, and priced well below Walloon ten minutes away.
links: Tip of the Mitt Watershed Council
Tip of the Mitt Watershed Council

lakes.name: Burt Lake
lakes.clarity: Good — the Watershed Council rates it a large, deep, high-quality lake. 73 ft max, 35 mi shoreline.
lakes.motors: Full motor, no cap; big enough to absorb traffic.
lakes.blurb: Michigan's fourth-largest inland lake, 17,436 acres in the middle of the Inland Waterway, with a state park, a big forested east shore, and prices far below the Torch/Walloon corridor. Room for five boats and then some.
links: Tip of the Mitt — Burt Lake

lakes.name: Mullett Lake
lakes.clarity: Very good — 145 ft max, 200 billion gallons, rated high-quality by the Watershed Council.
lakes.motors: Full motor, no cap.
lakes.blurb: 16,630 acres and 145 feet deep — Michigan's fifth-largest and, for its size, remarkably underdeveloped. Twenty-eight miles of shoreline, an Inland Waterway connection, and Cheboygan County prices. The best acreage-per-dollar on clear Michigan water.
links: Tip of the Mitt — Mullett Lake

lakes.name: Douglas Lake
lakes.clarity: Very good and improving — Secchi 10–14 ft; the Watershed Council notes it now borders on oligotrophy. 80 ft max.
lakes.motors: Full motor; low traffic, no town on the lake.
lakes.blurb: 3,727 acres wrapped by the University of Michigan Biological Station — a century of research, no commercial shoreline, no village, and the quietest big water in the northern Lower Peninsula. The closest thing Michigan has to a state-forest lake with private frontage on it.
links: Tip of the Mitt — Douglas Lake

lakes.name: Black Lake
lakes.clarity: Moderate; 50 ft max, more colored than its neighbors.
lakes.motors: Full motor; low traffic, state forest campground.
lakes.blurb: 10,130 acres of cheap frontage east of Onaway with state forest on part of the shore. Big and quiet; the water is ordinary. A value fallback.

lakes.name: Higgins Lake
lakes.clarity: Elite — Secchi 28.5–35 ft across the basins; 135 ft max, 21 mi shoreline. Michigan's clearest large lake alongside Torch.
lakes.motors: Full motor, no cap; two state parks and heavy summer boat traffic on weekends.
lakes.blurb: The clearest big water within five and a half hours of Chicago: 9,600 acres and Secchi readings in the thirties. The tradeoff is honest and significant — two state parks, a fully developed ring road, and midsummer Saturdays that feel like a lake in a metro area. Buy on the quiet north or east shore; frontage runs ~$1M–$1.9M.

lakes.name: Lake Margrethe
lakes.clarity: Moderate; 65 ft max.
lakes.motors: Full motor; Camp Grayling adjoins — expect occasional National Guard activity.
lakes.blurb: 1,920 acres outside Grayling with state land and the Camp Grayling reservation on part of the shore. Cheap, quiet on weekdays, and not archetype-clear.

lakes.name: Hubbard Lake
lakes.clarity: Good, not elite — Secchi around 12 ft; 97.5 ft max.
lakes.motors: Full motor, no cap; very low traffic.
lakes.blurb: 8,850 acres and nearly 100 feet deep in the empty northeast corner of the Lower Peninsula — big, deep, quiet, and dramatically cheaper than anything on the Lake Michigan side. Twelve-foot clarity is the honest limit; the value is not.

lakes.name: Grand Lake
lakes.clarity: Good; spring-fed, shallow-to-moderate depth.
lakes.motors: Full motor; almost no commercial development.
lakes.blurb: 5,660 spring-fed acres on the Presque Isle peninsula, minutes from two Lake Huron lighthouses and essentially undiscovered by the Chicago market. Cheap, quiet, and genuinely remote.

lakes.name: Chicaugon Lake
lakes.clarity: Excellent and improving — 115 ft max, among the deepest lakes of its size in the UP.
lakes.motors: Full motor, no cap; low traffic year-round.
lakes.blurb: 1,100 acres and 115 feet deep outside Iron River — the UP's best-kept clear-water secret, with improving Secchi trends, an active property owners association, and prices that would embarrass Vilas County. Under the size bar; over-delivers on everything else.

lakes.name: Cisco Chain of Lakes
lakes.clarity: Moderate to good; Thousand Island Lake is the deepest at ~40 ft, most basins are shallower.
lakes.motors: Full motor throughout; 15 connected lakes and 270 miles of shoreline — the largest connected chain in this report.
lakes.blurb: Fifteen connected lakes, 4,025 acres and 270 miles of shoreline straddling the state line at Watersmeet — you can run a boat all day and not repeat a bay. Substantially Ottawa National Forest shoreline. Shallow enough that the water colors by August; the cruising is unmatched anywhere in the Midwest.

lakes.name: Lake Gogebic
lakes.clarity: Moderate; 38 ft max — big but shallow.
lakes.motors: Full motor; state park landing, very low traffic.
lakes.blurb: The UP's largest inland lake at 13,380 acres, ringed by Ottawa National Forest and state park, with almost no development and the lowest waterfront prices per foot in this report — roughly 400 ft of raw east-shore frontage is live at $595K. Shallow water is the tradeoff.

lakes.name: Lake Michigamme
lakes.clarity: Weak — Secchi 7–8 ft; tannin-stained.
lakes.motors: Full motor; islands and rock, very low traffic.
lakes.blurb: 4,292 acres of dramatic rock-and-pine country west of Marquette. Spectacular setting, genuinely poor clarity. Listed for honesty: the sweep's best scenery-to-water-quality mismatch.

lakes.name: Lake Independence
lakes.clarity: Moderate; shallow.
lakes.motors: Full motor; a mile from Lake Superior at Big Bay.
lakes.blurb: 1,860 acres at Big Bay, twenty minutes from Lake Superior and about as far from Chicago as this brief allows. Remote, cheap, and not clear.

lakes.name: Brevoort Lake
lakes.clarity: Moderate; shallow (~30 ft).
lakes.motors: Full motor; Hiawatha National Forest shoreline.
lakes.blurb: 4,233 acres inside the Hiawatha National Forest west of St. Ignace — nearly all federal shoreline, so private frontage is rare and cheap when it appears. Shallow, stained water.

lakes.name: Les Cheneaux Islands
lakes.clarity: Excellent — Lake Huron water, cold and clear, in a sheltered 36-island archipelago.
lakes.motors: Full motor; protected channels mean flat water most days. This is Great Lakes water, not an inland lake.
lakes.blurb: The outlier and, for some groups, the answer: 36 islands and a dozen sheltered channels on northern Lake Huron, with a century-old wooden-boat culture, no crowds, and cottage prices a third of Torch Lake's. A private island with 575 ft of frontage and a three-stall boathouse is live at $1.0M. The catch: Great Lakes weather, a shorter season, and seven hours of driving.

lakes.name: Manitowish Waters Chain
lakes.clarity: Mixed across the ten basins — Rest and Spider are clear, the flowage arms are stained.
lakes.motors: Full motor throughout; ten connected lakes, the most navigable chain in Vilas County.
lakes.blurb: Ten connected lakes and roughly 3,800 acres in the northwest corner of Vilas County — genuine all-day cruising, a village with a grocery and an airstrip, and inventory that actually moves. The chain's water is good, not great; buy on Rest or Spider, not the flowage arms.

lakes.name: Kentuck Lake
lakes.clarity: Moderately clear; shallow (~26 ft).
lakes.motors: Full motor; Chequamegon-Nicolet National Forest shoreline.
lakes.blurb: 958 acres in the national forest east of Eagle River with federal land on much of the shore. Shallow, but almost undeveloped and cheap.

lakes.name: Little St. Germain Lake
lakes.clarity: Moderate; four connected bays, weedier than Big St. Germain.
lakes.motors: Full motor; connected to Big St. Germain.
lakes.blurb: 987 acres in four bays with a dense cottage shore. Included for market depth rather than water quality.

lakes.name: Boulder Lake
lakes.clarity: Clear; NHAL State Forest lake.
lakes.motors: Full motor; forest landing only.
lakes.blurb: 542 clear acres inside the state forest just north of Trout Lake. Under the size bar, but the frontage that exists here is the closest anyone gets to owning on the archetype cluster.

lakes.name: Clear Lake (Oneida)
lakes.clarity: Clear, as advertised; spring-fed.
lakes.motors: Full motor; very low traffic.
lakes.blurb: 470 acres of genuinely clear water near Lake Tomahawk. Well under the size bar; a strong second lake for a Tomahawk purchase.

lakes.name: Moen Chain
lakes.clarity: Moderate across four connected basins.
lakes.motors: Full motor; connected chain.
lakes.blurb: Four connected lakes north of Rhinelander with reasonable cruising and prices below the Minocqua belt. Ordinary water.

lakes.name: Whitefish Lake
lakes.clarity: Clear; deep basins.
lakes.motors: Full motor.
lakes.blurb: 800 clear acres south of Hayward with a quiet residential shore. Under the size bar; good water and good value.

lakes.name: Middle Eau Claire Lake
lakes.clarity: Clear, sand-bottomed.
lakes.motors: Full motor; part of the three-lake Eau Claire chain.
lakes.blurb: 880 sand-bottomed acres in far Bayfield County — the best of the Eau Claire basins, and among the cheapest clear water in the state.

lakes.name: Upper St. Croix Lake
lakes.clarity: Moderate; shallow.
lakes.motors: Full motor; headwater of the St. Croix National Scenic Riverway.
lakes.blurb: 856 acres at the head of the St. Croix Riverway. Historic setting, ordinary water, and about as far west as this brief reaches.

lakes.name: Lake Lucerne
lakes.clarity: Clear; 65 ft max, spring-fed.
lakes.motors: Full motor, no cap; Nicolet National Forest shoreline.
lakes.blurb: 1,000 clear, deep acres in the Nicolet north of Crandon, with federal forest on much of the shore and essentially no Chicago awareness. Pairs with Lake Metonga fifteen minutes away.

lakes.name: Roberts Lake
lakes.clarity: Moderately clear.
lakes.motors: Full motor.
lakes.blurb: 470 acres near Crandon with low prices and low traffic. Under the size bar; a value satellite to Metonga.

lakes.name: Lake Noquebay
lakes.clarity: Moderate; 51 ft max but weedy bays.
lakes.motors: Full motor, no cap.
lakes.blurb: 2,400 acres at four and three-quarter hours — the second-closest big ski lake in the report after Pelican. The water is ordinary and the shoreline unconserved; a drive-time play only.

lakes.name: Green Lake (Interlochen)
lakes.clarity: Very good — 100 ft max, clear and spring-fed.
lakes.motors: Full motor; Interlochen State Park landing is the only public access.
lakes.blurb: 1,980 acres and 100 feet deep beside Interlochen Center for the Arts — clear, deep, five hours from Chicago, and consistently overlooked by buyers fixated on Torch. Summer concerts drift across the water, which most groups count as a feature.

lakes.name: Thumb Lake (Lake Louise)
lakes.clarity: Elite — one of Michigan's clearest, ~90 ft deep, spring-fed.
lakes.motors: Full motor; tiny landing, almost no traffic.
lakes.blurb: 470 acres of exceptionally clear, 90-foot-deep water in the Boyne highlands. Far under the size bar and included on water quality alone — if the group would trade running room for clarity, tour it.

lakes.name: Bear Lake (Manistee)
lakes.clarity: Moderate; shallow (~50 ft) and warmer.
lakes.motors: Full motor, no cap.
lakes.blurb: 1,745 acres at four and three-quarter hours with a village on one end. Cheap, boat-friendly, ordinary water.

lakes.name: Arbutus / Spider Lakes chain
lakes.clarity: Good; small connected lakes in the Pere Marquette State Forest.
lakes.motors: Full motor on Arbutus; the chain narrows are no-wake.
lakes.blurb: A small chain inside the state forest twenty minutes from Traverse City. Too small for five boats; notable for the forest setting and prices a third of Torch's.

lakes.name: Paradise Lake
lakes.clarity: Weak — 1,900 ac but only ~10 ft deep.
lakes.motors: Full motor; very low traffic.
lakes.blurb: 1,900 acres of very shallow water near Carp Lake. The cheapest frontage in Emmet County by a wide margin, and the reason why.

lakes.name: Munuscong Bay / St. Marys
lakes.clarity: Moderate; shallow river-system water.
lakes.motors: Full motor; freighter channel nearby.
lakes.blurb: The St. Marys River system south of Sault Ste. Marie — big water, cheap frontage, and freighters on the horizon. Not the archetype; excellent for a group that wants a working Great Lakes view.

lakes.name: Hagerman Lake
lakes.clarity: Clear; Ottawa National Forest lake.
lakes.motors: Full motor; national forest landing.
lakes.blurb: 640 clear acres in the Ottawa National Forest outside Iron River, with a live 7-acre waterfront parcel at $425K. Under the size bar; the price-per-acre of clear UP water is the story.

lakes.name: Fortune Lakes
lakes.clarity: Clear; three connected basins.
lakes.motors: Full motor; connected chain, very low traffic.
lakes.blurb: Three small connected clear lakes in Iron County. Nowhere near the size bar, but representative of what $150K–$400K buys in the western UP.

lakes.name: Millecoquins Lake
lakes.clarity: Moderate; shallow and tannin-tinted.
lakes.motors: Full motor; almost no development.
lakes.blurb: 1,275 acres near Naubinway with a shoreline that is largely state and federal land. Remote and cheap; the water is bog-influenced.

lakes.name: Deer Lake (Boyne)
lakes.clarity: Good; small and clear.
lakes.motors: Full motor; small landing.
lakes.blurb: 500 clear acres at Boyne City, ten minutes from Lake Charlevoix's South Arm. Under the size bar; a credible satellite purchase.

listings.name: Moose Jaw Resort, Round Lake — $2.75M
listings.detail: 17 ac in the Chequamegon National Forest; working cabin cluster + lodge building
listings.fit: The thesis in one listing: a grandfathered multi-cabin cluster, already zoned for it, on a 3,294-acre clear ski lake ringed by national forest. Tour this first.

listings.name: Coady's Point of View Resort, North Twin — $2.8M
listings.detail: Resort + campground on the Twin Lakes chain; family-run since 1897
listings.fit: 129 years of grandfathered use on 2,871 acres of Class-A water. Keep six cabins, retire the campground, and you have the sketch.

listings.name: 11400 Santo Rd, Arbor Vitae — $3.25M
listings.detail: 34.5 ac; multiple year-round dwellings and cottages, rental-capable
listings.fit: Thirty-four acres and a multi-dwelling permit history — the density is the asset. The lake (busy Big Arbor Vitae) is the compromise.

listings.name: Buckatabon Lodge & Campground — $3.75M
listings.detail: 32.97 wooded ac, 459 ft sand shoreline on Lower Buckatabon Lake; lodge + cabins + campground
listings.fit: Over budget, but the clearest picture of what a licensed Northwoods resort conveys: grandfathered cabin density on sand frontage. Worth a calibration tour.

listings.name: Legacy lakefront estate, Lake Tomahawk — $3.3M
listings.detail: 1.45 ac, 338 ft frontage; maintained main home, furnished cabins, multiple docks
listings.fit: Exactly the program — lodge, cabins, docks — on 3,392 acres of 84-ft-deep clear water. Stretch pricing; the closest turnkey answer in Wisconsin.

listings.name: Pelican Lake resort — $724.9K
listings.detail: ~9 ac with 204 ft of frontage; cabin cluster
listings.fit: Under $750K for nine acres and a cabin cluster on 3,585 acres of ski water at five hours flat. Budget for a full rebuild; the entitlements are the buy.

listings.name: Pine Valley Lodge, Rhinelander — $1.5M
listings.detail: 27 ac with 1,900 ft of direct frontage on the Moen Lake Chain; historic lodge, rec hall, cabins
listings.fit: Twenty-seven acres and 1,900 feet of chain frontage for $1.5M — on pure frontage-per-dollar, the best land basis in the sweep. Moen's water is ordinary; the entitlements and the shoreline are not.

listings.name: Northern Michigan cabin resort (Herendeene Lake) — $2.5M
listings.detail: 430–450 ft frontage; hand-hewn 5BR log home + 6BR farmhouse + 6 remodeled cabins
listings.fit: Literally lodge + 6 cabins, between Sleeping Bear and Traverse City — BUT Herendeene is a 40-acre no-motor pond. Program 10/10, water 2/10. Tour it to calibrate, buy only with eyes open.

listings.name: Halfway Lake Cottages, Newberry — $1.595M
listings.detail: 25 ac, ~1,700 ft frontage; 8 cabins + guest house + 3BR owner's residence + pole barn
listings.fit: Eight cabins, a guest house and a lodge for $1.6M — the single best program-per-dollar found anywhere. The lake is private and no-motor: keep the boats an hour south, or pass.

listings.name: Houghton Lake cabin resort — $1.19M
listings.detail: 7 cabins + 2 homes on 150 ft of frontage
listings.fit: Nine buildings for $1.19M, forty minutes from Higgins. Houghton Lake itself is 20,000 shallow, busy acres — a program-first, lake-second fallback.

listings.name: Crooked Lake Resort, Lake MI — verify price
listings.detail: Owner's home + 6 winterized log cabins + park model + bait store on 146 ft of sand
listings.fit: Six winterized log cabins with fireplaces and a large owner's home — the turnkey version of the program at roughly 4:15 from Chicago. Small lake; confirm price and frontage with the broker.

listings.name: Lac du Lune assemblage — $1.35M
listings.detail: 27+ ac with 1,181 ft of frontage on clear water
listings.fit: The largest single-owner frontage assemblage found in Vilas County: 1,181 ft is enough for a lodge and five separately-lotted cabins under county shoreland math. Build the sketch exactly.

listings.name: Dunn Lake parcel, Presque Isle — $347.5K
listings.detail: 14+ ac with over 1,000 ft of lake frontage
listings.fit: A thousand feet of frontage for under $350K. Dunn is too small to ski — pair it with a slip on Presque Isle Lake five minutes away and you have a cheap, legal compound.

listings.name: Star Lake (Sawyer Co.) — 646 ac — $3.8M
listings.detail: 646± ac surrounding a 105-ac lake; the only private land on the water
listings.fit: Own the entire shoreline of your own lake — 646 acres, no neighbors, ever. Too small for towsports; the ultimate privacy play if the group will keep boats elsewhere.

listings.name: Amik Lake parcel + cabin, Lac du Flambeau — $305K
listings.detail: 31.85 wooded acres with an existing cabin
listings.fit: Thirty-two acres and a standing cabin for $305K. Cheapest acreage-plus-structure in the sweep; verify frontage and reservation title questions before anything else.

listings.name: East shore frontage, Bergland — $595K
listings.detail: ~400 ft of undeveloped frontage on the UP's largest inland lake
listings.fit: Four hundred raw feet on 13,380 acres for $595K — the cheapest big-lake frontage found. Shallow water and a seven-hour drive are the price.

listings.name: 28278 Fence Lake Rd, Michigamme — verify price
listings.detail: 14.2-ac private waterfront sanctuary, Baraga County
listings.fit: Fourteen private acres in the most dramatic country in this report. Clarity is the weak point; confirm price and frontage with the listing office.

listings.name: Hagerman Lake Rd, Iron River — $425K
listings.detail: 7.07 ac lakefront, Iron County MI
listings.fit: Seven waterfront acres for $425K, twenty minutes from Chicaugon's 115-ft-deep water. UP pricing is the whole argument for the western route.

listings.name: Iron County lakefront parcel — $129.9K
listings.detail: 3.49 ac with ~367 ft of frontage
listings.fit: Under $130K for 367 feet of frontage. Assemble two or three of these and the land basis for a five-cabin compound is under $400K.

listings.name: 6024 Black Oak Lake Rd S — $699K
listings.detail: 3BR/2BA year-round home on Wisconsin's clearest lake
listings.fit: One of very few homes that trade on Black Oak in any year. A beachhead on the best water in the state; add cabins on an adjacent lot as they surface.

listings.name: 12391 W Moreland Rd, Hayward — $1.95M
listings.detail: Furnished lakeside cabin + guest cottage; sugar-sand frontage, sunset exposure
listings.fit: Two dwellings already standing on 3,294 acres of clear ski water. The cleanest two-building start in Wisconsin; add cabins behind the setback line.

listings.name: Lac Courte Oreilles legacy estate — $2.495M
listings.detail: 10.82 ac with 320 ft of level, sandy shoreline
listings.fit: Eleven acres and 320 feet of sand on 5,039 acres of clear water. Enough land to cluster five cabins uphill of the 75-ft setback. Check reservation title carefully.

listings.name: Grindstone chalet + guest cottage — verify price
listings.detail: 805 sf 4-season chalet + 764 sf 3-season guest cottage; level lot, sand beach
listings.fit: Two buildings already on the best Secchi readings in this report. Small structures, big water — the classic Grindstone entry. Confirm price with the Hayward brokers.

listings.name: High Lake 5BR — $1.025M
listings.detail: 5BR/3.5BA on the High–Fishtrap chain between Land O'Lakes and Boulder Junction
listings.fit: A house that already sleeps most of the group, deep in the state forest belt, for a million dollars. Add two cabins and you are done.

listings.name: Chain Lake, Sugar Camp — $1.499M
listings.detail: 201 ft of frontage on the five-lake Sugar Camp chain
listings.fit: Chain access with real cruising forty minutes from Rhinelander. Frontage is thin for a five-dwelling program; treat it as the lodge and buy a neighbor.

listings.name: Phelps Class-A assemblage — $5.249M
listings.detail: 61+ ac with 1,022 ft of ripple-sand frontage
listings.fit: Well past budget, but it is the benchmark: sixty-one acres and a thousand feet of sand on Class-A musky water. Tour it to learn what the ceiling looks like.

listings.name: Phelps 6.95-ac, 500-ft frontage — $3.15M
listings.detail: 6.95 ac with 500 ft of ripple-sand frontage
listings.fit: Five hundred feet of sand — enough frontage for two principal dwellings plus guest houses under Vilas County math. The most executable stretch play in the county.

listings.name: 49945 N Lake Owen Dr, Cable — $3.0M
listings.detail: 5.31 ac, 350 ft of frontage, 4BR/3BA, 3,735 sf
listings.fit: The showpiece on 24.6-ft-Secchi water. Priced like Torch Lake; five acres is enough to cluster cabins behind it if the group stretches.

listings.name: Lake Namakagon inventory — $225K–$750K
listings.detail: Multiple lots and homes across the range, Cable WI
listings.fit: The assemblage lake: several sub-$750K parcels and homes live at once on 2,897 national-forest acres. Two adjacent purchases beat one big one here.

listings.name: 3285 S East Torch Lake Dr, Bellaire — $999K
listings.detail: 14+ ac, 4BR/3BA between Torch and Elk
listings.fit: Fourteen acres in the Torch–Elk corridor for under a million — rare, and enough land for the cabin cluster. Confirm which water the frontage is on.

listings.name: Torch Lake estate parcel — 7.5 ac
listings.detail: Rare 7.5-ac estate parcel between Torch and Elk Lakes
listings.fit: Seven and a half acres in the most supply-constrained corridor in the Midwest. Price on application; treat as a build-from-scratch canvas.

listings.name: 3151 Crystal Dr, Beulah — $1.9M
listings.detail: 4BR/3.5BA, 2,750 sf on 0.72 ac
listings.fit: Turnkey on the clearest big water in Michigan — but 0.72 acres means the cabins go on a second parcel. Buy it as the lodge and keep shopping the block.

listings.name: 4354 Crystal Dr, Beulah — $1.2M
listings.detail: 2BR/1.5BA, 1,147 sf on 0.34 ac
listings.fit: The cheapest frontage on Crystal this summer. A small cottage on a small lot — value is entirely in the water and the address.

listings.name: 7953 S Glen Lake Rd, Glen Arbor — $2.995M
listings.detail: 6BR/6.5BA, 4,854 sf on 0.58 ac inside Sleeping Bear
listings.fit: Sleeps the whole group day one on the prettiest water in this report. Sub-acre lot: this is a lodge purchase, not a compound.

listings.name: 5760 W Crystal View Rd, Glen Arbor — $1.995M
listings.fit: Nearly five acres in Glen Arbor for under $2M — the land, not the house, is the asset. Confirm frontage versus view.

listings.name: 6970 W Higgins Lake Dr — $1.45M
listings.detail: 6BR/1.5BA, 2,150 sf on prime west-shore frontage
listings.fit: Six bedrooms on the clearest big lake in the region for $1.45M. One and a half baths is the renovation line item; the water is the point.

listings.name: 303 Kenwood, Roscommon — $1.55M
listings.detail: 5+ wooded acres with sunset lake views
listings.fit: Five acres is enough for the whole cabin cluster — but confirm whether this is frontage or view before it goes further.

listings.name: West-shore 6BR, 100+ ft frontage — $1.9M
listings.detail: 6BR/1.5BA with over 100 ft of prime Higgins frontage
listings.fit: The top of the ordinary Higgins market: six bedrooms and a hundred feet of the clearest water in Michigan.

listings.name: South Arm estate parcel — 3.4 ac / 277 ft
listings.detail: 3.4 ac with 277 ft of South Arm frontage
listings.fit: The South Arm arbitrage: ~$2,450/ft median here against $7,000–$12,000/ft on the main basin. Price on application.

listings.name: 651 South Shore Dr, Walloon — $7.7M
listings.detail: 1.53 ac on the lake Hemingway wrote about
listings.fit: Included to calibrate, not to buy: this is what archetype water costs in Michigan when the culture never sells. Walloon's twelve listings totalled $64.7M.

listings.name: Private island cottage, Snows Channel — $1.0M
listings.detail: Own private island, 575 ft of waterfront, 3BR historic cottage, 3-stall boathouse, turret, gazebo
listings.fit: WILDCARD: your own island with 575 feet of Lake Huron frontage and a three-stall boathouse for a million dollars. Season is short and the drive is seven hours; nothing else in this report is remotely like it.

listings.name: Cedarville historic cottage — $799K
listings.detail: 4BR (incl. annex), 2.5BA, boathouse, sandy beach + acreage across the street with pole barn
listings.fit: A cottage, an annex, a boathouse and a back lot with a barn for $799K — the assemblage is already done. Great Lakes water, Great Lakes weather.

listings.name: Hessel turnkey waterfront — $579K
listings.detail: Fully furnished, refreshed spring 2026, transferable dock slip
listings.fit: Under $600K, furnished, with a dock slip that transfers. The cheapest way to test whether the group actually likes the Les Cheneaux.

listings.name: Cheboygan County lakefront inventory
listings.detail: ~1,000 ac of lakefront land listed countywide; average ask $376K
listings.fit: Cheboygan County land runs $12K–$17K/acre against Antrim's $18K–$28K. On Douglas, Burt and Mullett that gap is the whole strategy.

listings.name: Hubbard Lake inventory
listings.detail: Northeast Michigan's cheapest deep-water frontage; see Alcona County listings
listings.fit: 8,850 acres and 97 feet of depth at prices the Lake Michigan side hasn't seen in twenty years. Verify current inventory with an Alpena broker.

listings.name: Michigan DNR surplus land auction 2026
listings.detail: 97 statewide parcels, 20+ over 40 ac; Alpena/Cheboygan/Presque Isle counties Aug 21
listings.fit: The state sells surplus land every summer, much of it in exactly this corner. Register for the 2027 cycle now — this is how you buy 40+ acres at land value.

listings.name: Donner's Bay Resort, Turtle–Flambeau — $1.57M
listings.detail: 6 updated year-round cabins + owner's home + 1,500 sf bar & grill, Butternut WI
listings.fit: THE HEADLINE: six year-round cabins, an owner's lodge and a licensed bar, under $1.6M, on 12,942 acres of state Scenic Waters. The literal program, in budget, on genuinely wild water. Stained water is the only real objection.

listings.name: Butternut Lake resort — $849K
listings.detail: 2.70 ac with on-site dining and multiple cabins, direct lake access
listings.fit: Under $850K for a cabin cluster and a commercial kitchen. Butternut is a modest 1,000-acre lake — buy this for the buildings and the licence, not the water.

listings.name: 12770 Scenic Dr, Iron River — verify price
listings.detail: Lake Delta resort: main lodge with operating bar & restaurant, attached 3BR home
listings.fit: A full commercial lodge with a bar and a residence attached, in Bayfield County where land runs a third of Vilas prices. Confirm current ask and cabin count.

listings.name: 127 & 128 Oneida Dr, Houghton Lake — $1.5M
listings.detail: Turnkey waterfront hospitality: log cabins, owner's home, sandy shoreline
listings.fit: A second complete Houghton Lake cluster at $1.5M. Same verdict as the first: the program is right, the lake (20,000 shallow, busy acres) is not the archetype.

listings.name: Rockwell Lake Lodge, Luther — $6.2M
listings.detail: 670 ac with a private lake and a 12,000 sf lodge
listings.fit: Far past budget and included as the ceiling: 670 acres and your own lake, four hours out. Worth one calibration visit to see what a finished private-lake compound actually feels like.

listings.name: 8928 N Boot Lake Rd, Manistique — $650K
listings.detail: Furnished lodge sleeping up to 18, on 1.77 wooded acres
listings.fit: Sleeps eighteen, furnished, for $650K. The cheapest way in this report to house all five couples under one roof on day one — then add cabins as budget allows.

listings.name: Free Soil seven-cabin resort — $565K
listings.detail: 7 vintage cabins on 2.33 ac
listings.fit: Seven standing cabins for $565K, forty minutes from Hamlin Lake. Not waterfront — but as a source of grandfathered buildings to relocate or to learn from, it is instructive.

listings.name: Lupton lakefront resort — $950K
listings.detail: 5 ac; bar, commercial kitchen with pizza oven, guest docking, electric campsites
listings.fit: Five waterfront acres, a commercial kitchen and guest docking under $1M in Ogemaw County. Ordinary water; extraordinary entitlements per dollar.

listings.name: Torch Lake motel & cabins — $1.6M
listings.detail: Two adjoining parcels; fully updated 14-unit motel near the sandbar
listings.fit: Fourteen units of grandfathered density on the Midwest's most beautiful water. It is a motel by the sandbar, not a hushed compound — but the density is nearly impossible to replicate.

listings.name: Torch–Elk estate parcel — 7.5 ac
listings.detail: Rare 7.5-ac estate parcel between Torch and Elk Lakes
listings.fit: Seven and a half acres in a corridor that essentially never releases land. Price on application; the acreage is the product.

listings.name: 1350 S Hill Island Rd, Cedarville — vacant 150 ft
listings.detail: 150 ft of vacant waterfront just east of Cedarville
listings.fit: Vacant Les Cheneaux frontage — rare, and the cheapest route into the archipelago if the group prefers to build. Confirm price and septic feasibility.

listings.name: Hayward — 16154 US Hwy 63 — $975K
listings.detail: Hayward-area property via JMDS Properties
listings.fit: A Hayward listing from the region's dedicated resort brokerage — worth a call regardless, because JMDS is the desk that sees Sawyer County cabin clusters before MLS does.

listings.name: Chippewa Flowage inventory — 17 live
listings.detail: 17 active Chippewa Flowage listings in Hayward this summer
listings.fit: Seventeen live listings on 15,300 acres with 200 miles of shoreline that can never be developed. The deepest inventory-to-wildness ratio in the report.

listings.name: Presque Isle inventory — 30 live, avg $520K
listings.detail: 30 active Presque Isle lake listings; range $24.9K–$1.599M
listings.fit: Thirty live listings averaging $520K in the quietest township in Vilas County. This is where the assemblage strategy is most likely to actually work.

listings.name: Manitowish Waters chain inventory
listings.detail: Ten connected lakes; steady turnover of chain frontage
listings.fit: The chain trades more often than any archetype lake in Vilas County. If the group values cruising over clarity, start saved searches here.
